Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premium growth across our lines of business, elevated policy retention rates in our major product lines, disciplined combined ratio execution with clear forward guidance, and continuing improvements in customer acquisition cost trends that underscore our operational efficiency.

Emily, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.12 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included double-digit net written premium expansion, retention gains that stabilized our premium base, and underwriting discipline that kept our combined ratio at 96.2%, reflecting effective risk selection, claims management, and expense control. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with surplus of $12.5 billion and book value per share at $52.30, up 9% year-over-year.

Let me start with our top-line performance: net written premiums, or NWP, which grew 11.8% year-over-year to $8.7 billion. This marks our strongest quarterly NWP growth in over five years, powered by disciplined pricing, policy retention rates averaging close to 89% across the portfolio, and significant new business in high-margin segments. Excluding the impact of our mid-year acquisition of Midwest Specialty Risk Partners, organic NWP growth was a robust 9.4%, highlighting our commitment to rate adequacy amid ongoing inflation and social inflation challenges.

Breaking it down by line of business, personal lines saw +7.2% NWP growth to $3.2 billion. This delivered solid expansion after two years of double-digit gains. Homeowners and dwelling fire premiums rose 8.9%, supported by 5.1% average rate increases in catastrophe-exposed markets like Florida and Texas, where we've held 92% retention through targeted non-renewals of riskier coastal exposures—trimming our Florida book by 3% to refine our footprint. Auto premiums advanced a more modest 5.8%, facing some rate softening in California due to regulatory pressures post-Prop 103, but bolstered by our telematics program rollout, now spanning 1.8 million policies through our UnityDrive usage-based insurance platform. This has enhanced risk selection, with telematics participants showing 22% lower loss ratios. North America accounted for 85% of the growth, while our UK personal motor book increased 4% as claims frequency normalized post-COVID. Forward, we're committing $150 million to AI-powered pricing models to gain share in usage-based insurance, collaborating with InsurTech partners like Root and Hippo for embedded distribution opportunities.

Commercial property and casualty led with +15.6% NWP growth to $2.9 billion, capitalizing on the continued hardening of the P&C market—global commercial rates up 12% according to Verisk analytics. Middle-market packages jumped 17.2%, with new business up 24% from 9.8% rate hikes and robust demand in resilient sectors such as manufacturing and logistics. Workers' comp expanded 13.4%, our quickest pace in the segment, as payroll inflation enabled 6.5% earned rate gains; we've added parametric covers for labor shortages, following models like Chubb's innovations. Excess and surplus growth moderated to 11% amid reinsurance cost rises after events akin to Irma, but our quota-share treaties with reinsurers including Swiss Re have kept ceding commissions steady at 22%. U.S. commercial drove 70% of the increase, EMEA contributed 18% from UK and Benelux growth via our acquired broker network, and APAC added 12% despite softer Australian pricing. We're upgrading catastrophe modeling with RMS v17 to support $500 million more in Florida wind-exposed business without raising probable maximum losses.

Specialty lines accelerated +22.4% to $1.4 billion, serving as our growth engine through niche capabilities and favorable cycles. Cyber premiums surged 28.7% to $450 million, seizing opportunities from ransomware escalation—like Change Healthcare incidents—with standalone policies now 40% of the book at pricing levels comparable to IRMAA equivalents and 15% attachments. Directors and officers liability grew 19.2%, propelled by securities litigation amid interest rate pressures on public firms. Marine and aviation contributed 18%, boosted by Red Sea disruptions increasing hull and cargo needs. This growth is global: APAC cyber up 35% in Singapore and Japan, EMEA D&O solid in London, and U.S. marine aided by port congestion. Our advantage lies in a $200 million tech refresh with Duck Creek for real-time collateral monitoring, cutting unearned premium leakage by 15%. We've also achieved 12% cross-sell penetration of specialty into commercial accounts, emulating Berkshire Hathaway's approach.

Life and annuity rounded out at +6.8% NWP growth to $1.2 billion, providing stable diversification. Term life increased 7.5% via 4.2% rate tweaks and digital acquisition through our UnityLife app, now with 500,000 direct-to-consumer policies. Annuities leaped 9.1% to $650 million, capturing fixed indexed annuity demand with 5% Treasury yields—our MYGA products at 5.25% yields drawing volumes akin to Athene Holding. Health supplements grew 4%, hit by ACA competition, but Medicare Advantage partnerships in Sun Belt states added 10,000 lives. It's 95% North America-focused, with early EMEA expansion through Irish units. Ahead, we're considering Voya-style buys for scale in structured settlements.

Overall, ex-NWP growth was broad-based, with pricing adding 6.2 points, volume 4.1 points, and mix/retention 1.5 points. Our all-peril probable maximum loss remains flat year-over-year at $1.2 billion, thanks to 25% diversification into non-correlated areas like cyber and warranty. Inflation pressures persist—construction costs up 8% impacting homeowners—but our generalized linear models have embedded this in renewals. North America, 72% of NWP, grew 12.5%; EMEA 10.2% despite UK floods; APAC 8.9% on China easing.

Strategically, our TechFirst initiative includes $400 million in capex for generative AI underwriting, trimming cycle times 40%, and blockchain for reinsurance slips. We've divested $300 million in low-margin California auto to hit 15% ROE targets. Full-year NWP guidance is now $35.5-36.5 billion, implying 11-13% growth, with combined ratio tightening to 95.5%.

Retention remains the lifeblood of our P&C franchise. In Q3, our consolidated retention rate reached 87.2%, up 110 basis points year-over-year and 40 basis points from Q2. This is our 11th straight quarter of expansion, paying off from the multi-year Unity360 Customer Loyalty initiative, with over $250 million invested since 2022. We're past softer 2023 comparables from the hard market peak, when personal lines rates rose 15-20% amid Hurricane Ian and California wildfires.

By major product line: Personal auto, 40% of premiums, hit 88.5% retention, up 150 basis points year-over-year—our best in five years. A 22% enrollment surge in Snapshot telematics, like Progressive's model, now covers 35% of our auto book. Top safe drivers renew at 94%, versus 82% for high-risk. Northeast and Midwest held at 89-90%, aided by 12% higher bundling with homeowners. Florida and Texas dipped to 86% from litigated losses and roof inflation, challenges for Travelers and State Farm. UK auto reached 87% with IFRS 17 pricing and AI claims chatbots cutting cycle times 28%. We're rolling out Unity Drive AI in Q4 for predictive discounts, eyeing 2-3 point lift in 2025.

Homeowners/dwellers, 25% of premiums, achieved 92.1% retention, up 80 basis points. This stickiness comes from habitational risk mitigation, like fortified roof incentives with 15% uptake in cat zones. Loss-adjusted premiums grew 9% versus NAIC's 7% industry average. U.S. low-hazard states like Ohio and Pennsylvania averaged 93%, California 90% from wildfire constraints and ReinsureX exclusions. Spanish and Italian books renewed at 91% with parametric flood triggers post-Storm Celine. Asia-Pacific JV with Ping An hit 89% in Australia, offset by 18% multi-peril bundling amid cyclone costs. HomeGuard Smart IoT with Google Nest covers 28% of policies, speeding claims 40% and adding 300 basis points to retention.

Commercial lines SMB P&C, 20% of premiums, improved to 84.3%, up 200 basis points, though trailing personal due to bidding. We kept 91% of sub-$50K accounts via our digital portal slashing bind times 45%. Larger over-$250K held at 82% with pricing discipline as commercial rates softened 2-4% per Marsh. Southeast U.S. at 86% from workers' comp post-COVID; Midwest manufacturing 81% on supply chains. UK GL/liability 83% with Brexit endorsements; Canada 85% with cyber riders amid 35% ransomware rise per CyberCube. UnityBiz Pro API platform targets 87% next year, with ESG scoring like Chubb's.

Life and annuity, 15% of premiums, posted 89.7%, up 90 basis points, from low lapses in term and indexed universal life. VBT-17 tables and no-exam digital underwriting with Swiss Re boosted conversions 16%. U.S. group life 91%, individual 87%; German whole life 88% with Solvency II.

These gains shaved 3 points off our expense ratio to 28.2%, peer-leading. We guide 88%+ consolidated retention in FY 2025, assuming 1-in-50 year cats. Headwinds: auto repair inflation up 12% per CCC, Bermuda capacity softening. Our data flywheel with $150 million GenAI projects 150-200 basis points lift. We're gaining on direct writers like Lemonade in millennials, holding vs. Liberty Mutual in commercial.

As we look forward, let's discuss our combined ratio, the gold standard for underwriting profitability—losses plus expenses over earned premiums. Q3 came in at 96.8%, down 140 basis points from last year's 98.2%. Loss ratio improved 2.1 points to 68.4% on $145 million prior-year development in commercial auto and workers' comp, plus cats at 4.2 points versus 6.8%. Expense ratio steady at 28.4% despite VertexAI investments—wait, our UnityAI platform.

For Q4 2024, we guide 95.5% to 97.5%, sequential progress embedding 5-6 points normalized cats from Midwest/Southeast storms per RMS v18.1. Ex-cat attritional loss ratio 64-66%, backed by 8.2% personal and 7.5% commercial rates outrunning 5-6% loss costs from medical and repairs.

Full-year 2025 guidance: 96.0% to 98.0%, tightened from prior 96.5-99.0%. Loss ratio 67.5-69.5% accident-year ex-cat, with tailwinds from UnityAI live on 85% of $12.5 billion auto book using Cambridge Mobile Telematics data—15% loss cost drop for high-mileage like Progressive. Non-renewing $450 million California homeowners, shifting to Florida/Texas; cat exposure down to 22% of surplus. Reinsurance quota share on excess/surplus ceded 25% more at 15% lower cost from Bermuda like RenaissanceRe.

Expense ratio 28.0-29.0%, 40 basis points better: Guidewire Cloud phase 2 cuts claims 12-15% like Travelers; $60 million savings consolidating Duck Creek by mid-2025. EMEA reverts to 28.5% post-MiFID II; APAC cyber/D&O at 27.2%.

U.S. (65% of $28 billion earned premium) ex-cat 94-96%; Europe 98-100% on floods ($120 million reserved); Asia 92-94% on Japan motor growth. Our Underwrite to Win: 7-9% pricing, tech risk selection, cyber expansion via Unity Cyber Shield amid Chainalysis ransomware. 1:1.5 cat load, $4.2 billion tower buffers social inflation, climate. Positions for mid-teens ROE, $1.2 billion buyback.

Before questions, customer acquisition cost—or CAC—trends are a bright spot. CAC is fully loaded new policyholder cost: marketing, commissions, leads, onboarding over new policies. We target LTV/CAC over 4x.

Q3 blended CAC: $168 per new policy, down 15% year-over-year from $198, 8% sequential from Q1's $182. Sixth straight quarter compressing; trailing 12-month $175 below JD Power's $210 industry. Added 120 basis points to expense improvement for 92.4% combined amid California wildfires.

Digital DTC drove: $112 CAC, down 22%, from 35% conversion lift in mobile app/site. Programmatic on Google/Meta cut cost-per-click 18% targeting lapsed from Geico/Progressive. Agent/broker $285, flat, prioritizing embedded partnerships.

North America (72% new premium): $162 CAC, down 17%, from telematics (1.2 million users) boosting DTC auto 28%. UBI game-changer with AI pricing like Progressive. Europe $185, down 9%, UK Consumer Duty offset by Revolut bundles at 40% lower embedded. APAC $210 up 5% on India ad inflation, countered by vernacular AI chatbots cutting handoffs 45%.

Acquire Smart, Retain Smarter: $45 million YTD in GenAI quoting (OpenAI-like as Lemonade), down abandonment 32%. Embedded pilots with ride-sharing like Allstate/Uber target 50% CAC cut in mobility. Q4 guide: $158-162 blended, assuming ad stability. LTV/CAC 4.6x from 3.9x, auto churn 7.2% via EagleEye analytics—wait, UnityEye predictive. In 8% personal premium rise per AM Best, enables pricing discipline.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Alex Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the policy retention rates by major product line, particularly how you're addressing regional pressures?

David Reynolds: Good morning, Alex. As Emily detailed extensively, our 87.2% consolidated retention reflects broad strength, with personal auto at 88.5% driven by telematics and homeowners at 92.1% from IoT and mitigation. Regional pressures like Florida litigated losses are managed through personalization like Unity Drive AI and non-renewals where needed, positioning us for continued gains.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of persistent inflation and cat activity on your NWP growth and combined ratio guidance?

Emily Carter: Good morning, Maria. Inflation is embedded in our GLMs, contributing to 11.8% NWP growth with pricing outpacing costs. Cats are normalized at 5-6 points in Q4 guidance of 95.5-97.5%, and 96-98% for 2025, with reinsurance and portfolio shifts like California trims providing resilience. Our diversification keeps PML flat.

Operator: Our next question is from Jordan Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jordan Kim: Thanks. On customer acquisition costs, how sustainable is the compression, and any updates on embedded insurance pilots?

Emily Carter: Jordan, the 15% YoY drop to $168 is sustainable via GenAI quoting and digital channels, with LTV/CAC at 4.6x. Embedded pilots with fintechs and ride-sharing are scaling, targeting further 5-7% dips in Q4 and 50% reductions in mobility, outpacing peers' inflation.

Operator: Our next question from Chris Evans with Barclays.

Chris Evans: Good morning. Regarding combined ratio components, what gives you confidence in the loss ratio improvement?

Robert Kline: Good morning. Confidence stems from UnityAI's granular segmentation reducing costs 15%, reinsurance optimizations lowering ceding expenses, and portfolio actions trimming high-exposure like California homeowners. Rates exceeding trends support 67.5-69.5% ex-cat in 2025.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

David Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
